pr_title: Emit diagnostics for unsupported RDG scenarios
pr_body:
- Emit warnings for generics captured in parameters or response types (fixes https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/49384)
- Emit warnings for private/protected types captured in parameters or response types (fixes https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/47339)
- Fix warning for anonymous types in awaitable methods

issue_context.title: Request Delegate Generator fails to compile code with CS0246 error for endpoint with generic type parameter
issue_context.body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [X] I have searched the existing issues

### Describe the bug

I have an internal application that has a user interface where various properties of a configuration object can be changed independently. To reduce duplication for this operations, various HTTP PATCH endpoints with different URLs call through a generic method that maps the endpoint based on a code pattern.

The method is essentially this where boilerplate wraps the invocation of a delegate with a generic parameter:

```csharp
private static RouteHandlerBuilder MapRepositoryUpdate<T>(
    this IEndpointRouteBuilder endpoints,
    string pattern,
    Func<IConfigurationRepository, RepositoryId, T, CancellationToken, Task<bool>> operation)
{
    return endpoints.MapPatch(pattern, async (
        long installationId,
        long repositoryId,
        [FromBody] Payload<T> request,
        InstallationService service,
        IConfigurationRepository repository,
        CancellationToken cancellationToken) =>
    {
        if (!await service.UserHasAccessToRepositoryAsync(installationId, repositoryId))
        {
            return Results.NotFound();
        }

        await repository.EnsureRepositoryAsync(repositoryId, cancellationToken);

        return await operation(repository, new(repositoryId), request.Value, cancellationToken) switch
        {
            false => Results.Conflict(),
            true => Results.NoContent(),
        };
    }).RequireAuthorization();
}
```

When attempting to compile this application with the Request Delegate Generator enabled the compilation fails with the following errors:

```
src\MyApplication\Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.RequestDelegateGenerator\Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.RequestDelegateGenerator.RequestDelegateGenerator\GeneratedRouteBuilderExtensions.g.cs(43,118): error CS0246: The type or namespace name 'T' could not be found (are you missing a using directive or an assembly reference?) [src\MyApplication\MyApplication.csproj]
src\MyApplication\Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.RequestDelegateGenerator\Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.RequestDelegateGenerator.RequestDelegateGenerator\GeneratedRouteBuilderExtensions.g.cs(58,140): error CS0246: The type or namespace name 'T' could not be found (are you missing a using directive or an assembly reference?) [src\MyApplication\MyApplication.csproj]
```

It appears that the generator is not correctly taking into account the use of generics and is trying to use the identifier `T` literally as a type named `T` rather than as a generic parameter with that name.

When I tried to make the smallest repro I could with a one file application the endpoint would compile, so I think the issue may be related to the way the code is structured in the original application in terms of namespaces etc.

I've added an application that reproduces the error in [this repository](https://github.com/martincostello/rdg-generics-repro). There's probably more code that needed, but it's relatively minimal.

Note that the application will not actually run as I've stripped it down to just compiling so is 
missing various services registrations etc. It's just enough required to compile it successfully if the Request Delegate Generator is disabled.

### Expected Behavior

The application compiles and the endpoints behave at runtime as expected.


### Steps To Reproduce

1. Clone the [martincostello/rdg-generics-repro](https://github.com/martincostello/rdg-generics-repro) repository
2. Run `dotnet build`


### Exceptions (if any)

_No response_

### .NET Version

8.0.100-preview.6.23330.14

### Anything else?

_No response_
comments:
It looks like this might be a dupe of https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/47338.

We're punting this to .NET 9 since there are some things that need to be adjusted with the interceptors feature before we can accommodate this. For .NET 8, the plan is to fallback to runtime-based source generation for endpoints with type parameters.

review_comments: Should there be test(s) for emitting source for valid endpoints when invalid endpoints are also used? The diagnostic messages sort of imply that generation continues, and the messages could be suppressed technically.

> Should there be test(s) for emitting source for valid endpoints when invalid endpoints are also used?

Good recommendation.
Unless these are meant to be `else if`

> Unless these are meant to be else if

I debated this but I've always like the upfront disclosure you get when all the warnings are emitted at once instead of the progressive disclosure that allows you to keep fixing things until you get it right.

`SemanticModel` has an [`IsAccessible(Location, ISymbol)` method](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.codeanalysis.semanticmodel.isaccessible). I believe that is the intended way to check for accessibility instead of `DeclaredAccessibility` In the past, I've used it like this: `semanticModel.IsAccessible(0, symbol)`.

Have you used this in a generator? It seems like the API works by assessing accessibility within the context of an _existing_ syntax tree, but here we're trying to check accessibility in code we haven't generated yet.
Seems fragile? What if we emit info diagnostics, or diagnostics from a different part of the generator unrelated to this endpoint?

> What if we emit info diagnostics, or diagnostics from a different part of the generator unrelated to this endpoint?

At the moment, we're strictly using diagnostics as a way to indicate that some aspect of the endpoint is wrong and we can't statically generate it.

If we do decide to start emitting info-level diagnostics (I dunno how meaningful that would be for a source generator given that it's only visible in builds triggered from the IDE), we'd have to consider other aspects of the implementation, such as the way we use the lack of diagnostics to determine if we haven't been able to generate an endpoint.

All in all, I feel safe with the simplicity of `.Count > 0` here given the constraints were operating under compared to a more thorough check.
